clue.text: Swab interior of car carrying fish food

indicators.note: the swab is placed in the interior of the car, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a Rolls is a Rolls-Royce car
to swab a floor is to mop it; a mop is a swab

explanation.surface: Someone cleans out a car that has been ferrying a load of fish food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swab interior of car' reads as cleaning inside a vehicle; 'interior of' is really the container signal, and 'carrying' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollmops are rolled pickled herring fillets, eaten as a fish dish.

clue.text: After scramble for a ferry, thin out

indicators.note: a scramble is a jumbled mess, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: After a rush to catch the boat, the crowd disperses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rarefy is to make less dense, as air thins at altitude.

clue.text: Sexual urge of librarian taking marriage vow

parts.note: Lib is a short form for librarian
I do is the vow made at a wedding

explanation.surface: A librarian, saying the wedding vow, feels lust.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire or drive, in Freudian terms the energy of the sex instinct.

clue.text: Could seem an interminable time to Annie, commuting to factory

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: commuting means changing places, so Annie's letters are exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: The daily journey to the factory seems endless to a woman called Annie.
explanation.definitionFit: Millennia are periods of thousands of years, an almost endless stretch of time.

clue.text: Mean churchman holds one million letters of credit

indicators.note: the churchman holds the other pieces within him

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman
I is the Roman numeral for one
IOUs are written promises to pay, notes of credit

explanation.surface: A stingy cleric keeps a million in letters of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimonious means stingy, extremely unwilling to spend money.

clue.text: Bone fish with a letter opener

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, so take the start of letter

explanation.surface: Someone is told to bone a fish, using a letter opener as the knife.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpal describes a bone of the wrist; the carpals are the eight wrist bones.

clue.text: Including directions to range

parts.note: and means plus, including the next thing
E and S are the compass directions east and south

explanation.surface: Instructions on getting to a mountain range are included.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain chain running down western South America.

clue.text: In favour of having to pass through customs

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to go through customs at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'customs' looks like the border hall; it is the definition, meaning conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the official code of procedure and etiquette, accepted conventions of behaviour.

clue.text: Having taken note, catalogued quarters in occupation

indicators.note: the quarters occupy the catalogued list, sitting inside it

parts.note: listed means put in a catalogue
E and N are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: After noting things, someone has recorded the rooms that are occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: To have listened is to have paid attention, taken heed of what was said.

clue.text: Bone lad fractured on track provokes unseemly mirth

parts.note: a rib is one of the bones of the chest

indicators.note: a fractured thing is broken, so the letters of lad are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A boy breaks a bone on the railway line, and onlookers laugh coarsely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fractured' turns LAD into ALD; 'provokes' merely links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribaldry is coarse, vulgar humour, the kind that causes improper laughter.

clue.text: Start itching, covered in spots — apply iodine to the head? They are not all there!

parts.note: I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: one piece is covered by another, so the first letter of itching goes inside the spots

parts.note: dots are small spots

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rash begins to itch, leaving the sufferer covered in spots and dabbing iodine on their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the head' places the iodine at the front of DIOTS, the itching's I inside DOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be not all there is an idiom for being stupid or simple-minded, as fools are.

clue.text: Perch, perhaps, leaping in display of athletic skill?

parts.note: the perch, also called the rod, is an old measure of length equal to a pole
vaulting means leaping over something

explanation.surface: A bird's perch seems to be leaping like an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' suggests a fish or a bird's roost; it is the old unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole vault is a field event, a show of athletic prowess at the jump.

clue.text: Sweet nonsense

definitions.meaning: evasive talk or a dodge, as in fudging an issue

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a soft confection and evasive, waffling nonsense.

clue.text: Material that makes clubs match

parts.note: irons are golf clubs
to tone with something is to match or harmonise with it

explanation.surface: A golfer asks what fabric would make a bag that goes with the clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a sedimentary rock rich in iron, used as a material, also a type of hard pottery.

clue.text: English coppers soon taking over US surveillance equipment

indicators.note: the letters take over one another's places, being turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: British police are about to be supplanted by American spying gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: A snooperscope is an American infrared viewing device for seeing in the dark, used for spying.

clue.text: A lady's sad, recollecting times when she was young

indicators.note: recollecting can be read as re-collecting, gathering the letters again in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman feels melancholy remembering her youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad days is an idiom for one's youthful, inexperienced time of life.

clue.text: Raj lady's address one member has broadcast to British

annotationWithheld.why: Raj lady's address one member has broadcast to British: wordplay needs MEMSAHI plus B, but one member has gives I, M and HAS, leaving no source for the extra ME; possibly OCR garble, no other copy found
annotationWithheld.clue: Raj lady's address one member has broadcast to British

clue.text: Wade off course through Scottish river to racetrack

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go through the river, set within it

parts.note: the Spey is a river in Scotland

indicators.note: off course means wandering astray, so the letters of wade are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone strays while wading across a Scottish river towards a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedway is a motorcycle racing circuit, an oval track for that sport.

clue.text: Most definitely needing help, with calamity at sea

indicators.note: something at sea is confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A disaster in the ocean means help is very definitely needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something emphatically means with great force and certainty, without doubt.

clue.text: Ring again to withdraw

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a second time to cancel.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or rescind it, taking it back.

clue.text: Buzzed by unmanned aircraft and died

parts.note: a drone is a pilotless aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone was buzzed by a drone and was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: To drone is to hum monotonously, like a bee, so droned is a past tense of humming.

clue.text: Ejected from plane initially sent out with malfunctioning flue?

definitions.text: Ejected from plane initially sent out with malfunctioning flue?

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged
initially means take only the first letter of plane
a malfunctioning flue is not working properly, so its letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Something gets dumped from an aircraft because its exhaust pipe has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges P and SENT into SPENT; 'malfunctioning' rearranges FLUE into FUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Used-up fuel, burned or exhausted, could be the stuff dumped from an aircraft with a faulty exhaust.

clue.text: Wooden objects — half a score about to be included

indicators.note: the word for about is included inside the number

parts.note: a score is twenty, so half of it is ten
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Ten wooden items are counted, with a couple more about to be added.
explanation.definitionFit: Treen is small domestic ware such as bowls and spoons turned from wood.

clue.text: Gloomy depression beginning to lift

indicators.note: the beginning of depression is its first letter

parts.note: to rear is to raise or lift up

explanation.surface: A dark mood starts to clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal and cheerless.

clue.text: Cable was, sadly, received by girl

indicators.note: one piece is taken in by another, so the jumbled letters sit within the girl

parts.note: her refers to a girl or woman

indicators.note: sadly suggests something has gone wrong, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A telegram is unhappily taken in by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Capital article about Belgium's plant species

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
BE is the country code for Belgium
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A capital-city paper runs a piece about a Belgian plant variety.
explanation.definitionFit: The lima bean is a legume plant, Phaseolus lunatus, grown for its flat edible seeds.

clue.text: Barking cove, gin-sozzled

parts.note: a cove is a small bay

indicators.note: sozzled means drunk, so the letters of gin stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk fellow, a cove full of gin, is acting mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cove' looks like the old slang for a man; here it is the coastal inlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that is barking loudly and persistently is baying, as hounds do.

clue.text: Prods a youth to bring this food

parts.note: to egg someone on is to prod or urge them
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: Someone nudges a young man to bring along a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg salad is a dish of chopped hard-boiled eggs with mayonnaise, so it is a food.
